definitions.gloss: tidying up; organizing; putting things in order
definitions.explanation: the act of arranging items neatly and systematically, often used as a set phrase emphasizing thorough organization

notes:
A ⟦{四字熟語|よじじゅくご}→四字熟語：15663_yojijukugo⟧ combining ⟦{整理|せいり}→整理：03297_seiri⟧ (sorting, organizing — deciding what to keep) and ⟦{整頓|せいとん}→整頓：07617_seiton⟧ (arranging neatly — putting things in their place). Together they emphasize thorough organization.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {整理整頓|せいりせいとん}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to organize and tidy up
- {整理整頓|せいりせいとん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{行|い}き{届|とど}く→行き届く：30420_ikitodoku⟧: to be thoroughly organized
- {整理整頓|せいりせいとん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{苦手|にがて}→苦手：03513_nigate⟧: to be bad at organizing

CULTURAL NOTE:
Often seen on signs in schools and workplaces. {整理整頓|せいりせいとん} is considered a fundamental virtue in Japanese culture, taught from elementary school onward.

RELATED WORDS:
- {片|かた}づける: to tidy up (casual, everyday)
- ⟦{断捨離|だんしゃり}→断捨離：08348_danshari⟧: decluttering (modern concept, minimalism-oriented)
- ⟦{整理|せいり}→整理：03297_seiri⟧: organizing/sorting (used alone as well)
